new_statements.quote: 12 ACCENT.—A large proportion of the words in Bulu are monosyllables. Of the remainder, the greater part consists of words made up of a stem and a Noun Prefix. In such words the prefix has an accent of its own, being pronounced almost like a separate word; e.g., in é-bak, bi-bak, where the é- and bi- are prefixes, both syllables have a like stress. In the (comparatively few) words of more than one syllable without the prefix, the first syllable, or the first of the stem, has a strong accent, the one or more following being lightly pronounced, e.g.: yemeya — accent on yem; ndeñele — ndeñ; afô'ôlô — a-fô (the a being a noun prefix).

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (bulu1251 is not in the catalog and has no stress statement held by the project; all previously opened sources were tonal descriptions silent on stress). First explicit placement statement: stem-initial accent with separately accented noun prefixes, alongside lexical tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent is stem-initial: in polysyllables the first syllable of the stem carries a strong accent and all following syllables are lightly pronounced; a noun-class prefix is pronounced 'almost like a separate word' with an accent of its own, so in prefix+monosyllabic-stem words (e-bak, bi-bak) both syllables have 'a like stress', and in afo'olo the accent is marked on both the prefix a- and the stem-initial fo. Most words are monosyllables. Sec. 13 (p. 7) separately describes lexical tone (words spoken in a higher or lower tone than ordinary, distinguishing homonyms; 'many other words have their characteristic tones'), so Bulu is described as having both tone and a stem-initial accent; sec. 9 (p. 5) adds that unaccented vowels assimilate to the preceding accented vowel.
new_statements.secondary_stress: No graded secondary stress described; the noun prefix bears an accent 'of its own' equal to the stem-initial accent ('both syllables have a like stress'); post-initial stem syllables are 'lightly pronounced' (in Fang, per the note on p. 7, so lightly that their vowels reduce to obscure e).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated as exceptions. Scope notes: 'a large proportion of the words in Bulu are monosyllables'; words of more than one syllable without a prefix are 'comparatively few'. The note on p. 7 contrasts Fang (stronger reduction of unaccented syllables: bomolo -> Fang bomele) and Bene (afogele).
new_statements.identity_note: Bates 1904 describes Bulu as spoken around the American Presbyterian mission stations of south Cameroon (Efulen/Elat-Ebolowa area; vocabulary largely from Silas F. Johnson's MS); he contrasts Bulu with Fang and with the 'north dialects like Yewondo and Bene' (p. 4, p. 7 note), so the statement is about Bulu proper (bulu1251), not Fang or Ewondo. the copy consulted sits in the beti1250 folder only because an earlier hunt filed it there; the language described is Bulu.

new_statements.quote: Die größte Zahl der Worte im Bulu ist einsilbig. Von den übrigen bestehen viele aus einem einsilbigen Stamm mit vorgesetztem Präfix. Es ruht dann der Hauptton auf dem Präfix (é-lé Baum, mi-mbok Gefangene), während der Stamm (lé und mbok) einen leichteren Ton erhält. [...] In den verhältnismäßig wenigen Worten von mehreren Silben ohne Präfix hat die erste Silbe bzw., bei zusammengesetzten Worten, der erste Stamm den Hauptton. fuman jd. verfehlen, Betonung auf fum | diñesan einander lieben, „ „ diñ | ébañkelek Erdscholle, „ „ é und bañ [...] Der Tonfall ist fest mit dem Worte verbunden und ändert sich niemals [...]. Jede Silbe hat ihren eigenen Ton, der ihr dauernd erhalten bleibt.
new_statements.translation: The greatest number of words in Bulu are monosyllabic. Of the rest, many consist of a monosyllabic stem with a prefix placed before it. The main stress (Hauptton) then rests on the prefix (é-lé 'tree', mi-mbok 'prisoners'), while the stem (lé and mbok) receives a lighter accent. [...] In the relatively few words of several syllables without a prefix, the first syllable -- or, in compound words, the first stem -- has the main stress. fuman 'to miss someone', stress on fum | diñesan 'to love one another', [stress on] diñ | ébañkelek 'clod of earth', [stress on] é and bañ [...] The pitch pattern is firmly bound to the word and never changes [...]. Every syllable has its own tone, which it keeps permanently.
new_statements.citation: von Hagen, Gunther Tronje. 1914. Lehrbuch der Bulu-Sprache. Berlin: Radetzki. § 7 'Betonung und Tonlehre', pp. 13-14 (per DNB table of contents).

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record. bulu1251 has no catalog record and no existing stress statement; all sources opened in earlier passes (Wilkinson 1975, Yukawa 1992, Clem 2014, NDI 2001, Ze Amvela & Eno Belinga 1978, Alexandre & Binet 1958) describe Bulu as tonal (2-3 levels) and are silent on stress. von Hagen 1914 is the first opened source with an explicit placement: main stress on the first syllable (the noun prefix when present, else the first syllable / first stem), co-existing with fixed per-syllable high/low tone. Compatible with the tonal descriptions; adds the stress placement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bulu is described as a tone language (every syllable has its own invariable tone; p. 14: 'Der Bulu kommt beim Sprechen im Gegensatz zum Jaunde fast nur mit Hoch- und Tiefton.. aus' = Bulu manages with almost only high and low tone, unlike Yaunde) AND the author states a word-stress rule: most words are monosyllabic; in prefix + monosyllabic-stem words the main stress (Hauptton) falls on the prefix (é-lé 'tree', mi-mbok 'prisoners') with a lighter accent on the stem and a slight pause between prefix and stem; in the few prefixless polysyllables the first syllable carries the main stress (fuman -> fum, diñesan -> diñ); in compounds the first stem carries it (ébañkelek stressed on the prefix é and the first stem bañ). Net placement: word-initial (prefix-inclusive) main stress, i.e. fixed: initial syllable, alongside lexical high/low tone. Sentence emphasis may strengthen a word without altering its tone pattern; wrong 'Betonung durch Modulation der Stimme' makes speech unintelligible.
new_statements.secondary_stress: The stem after a stressed prefix 'erhält einen leichteren Ton' (receives a lighter accent), i.e. a weaker prominence on the stem syllable; in compounds both the prefix and the first stem are named as stressed (ébañkelek: 'é und bañ'). No further secondary-stress rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated as exceptions. Notes: a 'kleine, kaum merkliche Pause' between prefix and stem; nasal prefixes always carry their own tone (p. 77 fn., p. 84 fn.); a diphthong has only one tone (p. 76 fn.); Bulu lacks the finer pitch distinctions of Yaunde (Nekes 1911), so the author gives no tone transcription; § 3c p. 10 refers to 'der unbetonte Schlußvokal eines mehrsilbigen Wortes' (the unstressed final vowel of a polysyllable is reduced to a schwa-like quality before consonants), consistent with non-final stress.
new_statements.identity_note: von Hagen describes the Bulu of the German Kamerun Schutztruppe district in South Cameroon (drum names from the Yekombö, Yemven, Esaman, Yemvak, Yemfek clans; Sangmelima mentioned), written in the orthography and noun-class system of G. L. Bates 1904 / the American Presbyterian Mission at Elat (Ebolowa); he contrasts Bulu throughout with Jaunde (Ewondo, Nekes 1911). This is Bulu proper (bulu1251), not Beti/Ewondo, although the located file is stored under the beti1250 folder with a pointer line in bulu1251/.

sources.note: 'Au point de vue phonétique, la caractéristique la plus importante du groupe est sans doute l'emploi de tons.. Bates et Johnson reconnaissent cinq tons, plus le glissando du négatif. Bertaut, après les auteurs allemands, distingue deux tons fondamentaux — haut et bas — deux tons dérivés — ascendant et descendant — et un ton moyen'; rhythm said to matter in drum messages. sources.citation: Abomo-Maurin, Marie-Rose. n.d. [site dated 2019-]. Bulu. In: ELLAF - Encyclopédie des littératures en langues africaines (notice de langue), ISSN 2804-7672 (en ligne). Paris: ELLAF / Huma-Num. Web page.
sources.note: Short first-hand typological notice; under 'Caractéristiques linguistiques générales' it states verbatim: 'Le système phonologique du bulu compte 7 voyelles et 21 consonnes. Il distingue trois tons, haut, moyen et bas.' (three level tones H, M, L; no mention of contour tones, downstep or stress). This sides with the three-toneme analyses (Wilkinson 1975, Ze Amvela 1978) against the two-tone analyses (Alexandre 1966, Clem 2014) already listed here.
